reason: The pome is ovoid or subglobose. PATO_0001891 'ovate' has 'ovoid' as a synonym, and spheroid fits subglobose. The fruit bearer and 3-D shape are right. Once pato#627 is merged, ovoid could move to the 3-D temporary class.

fix: 'basal leaves' should ground to rosette leaf, not to the general class leaf.
reason: The flora says only young basal leaves are very hairy on both surfaces. Read as all leaves, the statement is wider than the source. The young context and 'usually' are right.
12–25(–30) teeth on each side of the lamina. The count, the extreme value of 30, the each-side position and the lamina container are all right.

fix: 'X not seen', 'X unknown' and 'X not known' mean there is no data. They are not absence and should produce no annotation.
reason: 'Fruit not seen' means the author had no fruiting material. It does not mean fruit is absent. The same sentence goes on to describe the fruiting pedicel.
'Young leaflets often have a lustrous quality': glistening (synonyms shiny, glossy) on the leaflet, with the young context and 'often'. All right.

target: involucral collar of Gnetum spike (no PO class; not leaf collar PO_0006012)
fix: In Gnetum, 'collar' means the involucral collar (ring of bracts) on the spike. The grass leaf collar is a different structure. Do not ground 'collar' to PO_0006012 outside grasses.
reason: The 55–70 count is right, but the flowers are male flowers on the involucral collars of the male spike. The container 'leaf collar' is wrong.
'Petiole ± pubescent': pubescent on the petiole, with ± read as 'approximately'. This matches the source.

fix: In 'acutish to short-acuminate at the base', the closing 'at the base' moves the quality onto the lamina base. The place phrase must be applied to the whole value range before it.
reason: The acutish-to-short-acuminate range is said of the blade base, not the whole leaf. The blade apex is described separately as short-acuminate.
The infructescence is an umbellate raceme, so a raceme is present. That is true, though 'umbellate' and the fruiting stage are not captured.
'Cyme many-flowered': flowers present in the inflorescence, with the amount 'many'. This matches the source.

fix: The 'ca.' qualifier could be kept as 'approximately'.
reason: The flora gives the corolla as ca. 5 cm, and the annotation matches. The source may have a typo (the upper lip is only 3.5 mm), but the annotation says what the source says.
'Leaflets ... sparingly strigose above' puts the strigose hairs on the upper (adaxial) side. The degree 'sparingly' is lost, but the statement stays true.

fix: 'sub-' (slightly, nearly) could be kept as a degree qualifier.
reason: The lateral sepals are subfalcate, i.e. slightly falcate. Falciform on the sepal is acceptable. The bearer could be narrowed to the lateral sepals.
Stamens 100–150. The count is right.
Leaf blade broadly elliptic or ovate, given as alternatives, with ovate as the temporary 2-D class. The rarer 'oblanceolate-elliptic' alternative is left out, but nothing stated is false.
'1 1 mm' is a scanning (OCR) split of 11 mm. Sepals 14 mm long, broadly elliptic and 11 mm wide is consistent.

fix: 'veins N per side' (also 'lateral veins N pairs') counts the secondary veins on each side of the midrib, not vascular bundles in general.
reason: 4 veins per side of the blade are the secondary veins. The count and the each-side position are right.
Stems yellowish to reddish brown, read as a colour continuum on the stem. The 'approximately' qualifier fits '-ish'.

fix: In 'A or B to C', the range runs from B to C. The relation must include the third value, C, not stop at 'A or B'.
reason: The capsule is glabrous, or between glabrate and sparsely puberulent. The annotation keeps only glabrous or glabrate and drops the sparsely puberulent end.

fix: In French, 'pauci- à multiflores' (and English 'few- to many-flowered') is a range from few to many. Do not read only the first prefix as the amount.
reason: The cymes are few- to many-flowered. The annotation records only 'few'.

target: bristle on the legume (no PO class)
fix: In a run of comma-separated qualities after 'Bristles on the legume ...', the qualities belong to the bristles, the subject, not to the part named inside the subject phrase.
reason: The subject is the bristles on the legume. 'Glabrous or pubescent with short spreading hairs, rarely retrorsely hispid' describes those bristles, which in Zornia can be barbed.

target: exostome (no PO class); stated as absent
fix: The exostome is a part of the peristome. 'Exostome absent' must not become a statement about the whole peristome, and above all not a positive one.
reason: The statement says the exostome is absent. The annotation turns it into 'peristome present'. The peristome is indeed single elsewhere in the text, but this statement does not say that.
Petals rounded at the apex: obtuse (synonym 'roundish') on the petal apex. This matches the usual reading.
Stems with usually 3 to 4 flowers. The count and 'usually' are right.
Leaves usually unlobed: lobed, negated, with 'usually'. This is right.
Flowers yellowish: yellow, with 'approximately'. This is right.

fix: 'testa' has its own PO class. It should not be folded into the seed.
reason: The flora says the testa is pitted. Foveate is the right quality, but the bearer is the testa.

target: position: median part of the floral scale
fix: 'laterally X, medially Y' gives colours for different zones of the same organ. The zone word must go in the position slot.
reason: The floral scales are light brown at the sides and green to brown only in the middle. Without 'medially', the annotation conflicts with the 'laterally light brown' statement.
Pericarp firm-carnose, i.e. firm-fleshy: fleshy on the pericarp. This is right.
Style shorter than the corolla tube: decreased length, compared with the corolla tube (FLOPO_0985018). This is right.
